land.text: the lower Syr Darya around Cend, left by Seljuk's clan when it broke with the Oghuz Yabghu

predecessors.note: The page: Seljuk, leader of his clan, broke with the Yabghu, the Oghuz supreme chieftain, and camped on the west bank of the lower Syr Darya. Cliopatria's Oghuz Turks row (750-1055) is the Yabghu state.

land.text: the Seljuk state after Dandanaqan (23 May 1040), with Khorasan won from the Ghaznavids

successors.note: Same state under another Cliopatria row: Cliopatria passes from 'Seljuk Dynasty' (to 1039) to 'Great Seljuk Empire' (from 1040); the Seljuk Empire page dates the formation to 1037 under Tughril and Dandanaqan to 1040. The Seljuk dynasty page instead says the empire was 'established' after the siege of Isfahan in 1050/51.

capitals.name: Cend (Jand), on the lower Syr Darya
capitals.note: Infobox 'Initial Dominion seat: Cend (985-1037)'. Coordinates are approximate (the ruins lie near the lower Syr Darya in Qyzylorda oblast); the gazetteer has no Jand.

capitals.name: Nishapur
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Tughril I declares Nishapur as capital' in 1037; the dynasty-wide list gives Nishapur 1037-1043 for the Great Seljuk line.

correction.text: Seljuk's clan on the west bank of the lower Syr Darya with its seat at Cend (Jand), from 985; shape unchanged from the 990 row, only the years are extended

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins in 990 but the page's infobox gives the initial seat at Cend from 985 and says 'Around 985, Seljuk and his clan converted to Islam'. The 990 shape is carried back five years unchanged.

291,684 km2: the lower Syr Darya strip from Jand (45.6 N) to the Turkistan reach, which fits the clan's camp on the west bank of the lower Syr Darya and the seat at Cend. The page gives no area; extent of the nomadic range is not on the page (unverified beyond the river).

Same shape as 990, 1000-1033. The page is internally uneven here: the infobox says 'Tughril I abandoned Cend' in 1016 and a footnote that Tughril and Chaghri 'had left Cend before 1016 with their tribe' and were nomadic until they served the Qarakhanids, yet the same infobox keeps Cend as the seat until 1037. Where the tribe lived in 1016-1034 is not on the page, so Cliopatria's strip stands unverified.

union.text: Cend (Jand) and the west bank of the lower Syr Darya, where Seljuk's clan camped
Dihistan, Nasa and Farawa, the three Khorasan cities Mas'ud ceded

correction.text: the Cend base on the lower Syr Darya plus Dihistan, Nasa and Farawa ('three cities in Khurasan: Dihistan, Nasa, and Farawa'); Khwarezm, Gorgan and Merv/Nishapur are not yet Seljuk

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1034-1039 shape (823,000 km2) adds Khwarezm (55%), the Turkmen plains and Golestan (94%) to Khorasan. The Dandanaqan page has the Seljuks sheltering in Khwarazm only 'under the advocacy of the Ghaznavid governor Harun' and fleeing after his murder in 1035, and Mas'ud giving them 'three cities in Khurasan: Dihistan, Nasa, and Farawa'; the Tughril page puts Gorgan and Tabaristan in 433 AH (1041-1042) and the Seljuk Empire page puts Merv and Nishapur in 1037-1038. The correction is for 1034-1036 only: the Jand base plus the three ceded cities; Merv and Nishapur come with the new 1037 keyframe.

correction.text: Nishapur, Merv and the Dihistan-Nasa-Farawa strip: the Khorasan the Seljuks held from 1037

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1037-1039: Tughril and Chaghri captured Merv and Nishapur in 1037-1038 and Nishapur became the capital in 1037 (Seljuk dynasty infobox); Cend, the old seat, is left behind. The Seljuk Empire page's 3.9 M km2 is for c. 1080 and does not apply to this stage; the corrected shape is about 0.35 M km2.

region.text: the west bank of the lower Syr Darya around Cend (Jand)

ledger.note: 985: Seljuk, leader of his clan, breaks with the Oghuz Yabghu and settles on the lower Syr Darya, with his seat at Cend. Seljuk, leader of his clan, broke with the Yabghu, the Oghuz supreme chieftain, and camped on the west bank of the lower Syr Darya; infobox 'Initial Dominion seat: Cend (985-1037)' and 'Around 985, Seljuk and his clan converted to Islam'. The year is the infobox's seat date, the break itself is undated.

region.text: the Nasa district of Khorasan, where the Ghaznavids were defeated in 1035

ledger.note: 1035: the Seljuks defeat the Ghaznavids at Nasa. 'The Seljuks defeated the Ghaznavids at the Battle of Nasa in 1035' (Seljuk dynasty); they had fled south after the Ghaznavid governor Harun of Khwarazm was assassinated in 1035 (Seljuk Empire page, which also has them driven out of Transoxiana around 1034-1035). The fight for Khorasan runs to Dandanaqan on 23 May 1040, recorded in the great-seljuk-empire ledger.

1035: Mas'ud cedes three Khorasan cities to the Seljuks. 'Mas'ud gave the Seljuks three cities in Khurasan: Dihistan, Nasa, and Farawa.' The page says only 'after the battle' (it is not dated; the Ghaznavid dossier places it in 1034 from the Ghaznavid page) and the year here is the Cliopatria shape's 1034. [Reviewer me-09-a, 2026-10-25: year 1034 -> 1035: the Battle of Dandanaqan page has the Seljuks settle in Khwarazm in 1034, flee to Nasa after Harun's murder in 1035, beat Iltughdi's army there, and only then 'Ma'sud entitled the Seljuk to three cities in Khurasan: Dihistan, Nasa, and Farawa'; confidence stays 1 (no year on the page).]
1037: Tughril makes Nishapur his seat. Infobox: '1037 - Tughril I declares Nishapur as capital'; a footnote says Cend was treated as the seat until 1037, when Tughril occupied Nishapur.
1037: Tughril and Chaghri take Merv and Nishapur. Tughril and Chaghri captured Merv and Nishapur in 1037-1038 (Seljuk Empire page); Nishapur is the seat from 1037 (Seljuk dynasty page).

region.text: Cend and the lower Syr Darya, the initial dominion

ledger.note: 1037: the old seat on the Syr Darya is left behind. The page keeps Cend as the seat to 1037 and then names Nishapur; it does not say who held the lower Syr Darya afterwards (Cliopatria's 1034 shape still contains it, the 1037 keyframe does not).

region.text: Khorasan, contested between the Seljuks and the Ghaznavids since 1035

ledger.note: 1039: the fight for Khorasan passes to the Great Seljuk row. The Seljuk Empire page dates the Seljuk victory at Dandanaqan to 1040 ('decisively defeated Masʽud I, forcing him to abandon most of his western territories'); the contest is closed in the great-seljuk-empire ledger on 23 May 1040. This end is set at the dossier's last year so the pair validates.

region.text: the Seljuk state continues as the Great Seljuk Empire

ledger.note: 1039: the Seljuk dynasty's own row ends and the Great Seljuk Empire follows. The Seljuk Empire page dates the formation under Tughril to 1037 and Dandanaqan to 1040; the cut at 1039|1040 is Cliopatria's, not the page's.

wars.name: Seljuk-Ghaznavid struggle for Khorasan (to Dandanaqan)
wars.outcome: Seljuk victories at Nasa (1035), then Merv and Nishapur (1037-1038); the Ghaznavids lose Khorasan at Dandanaqan on 23 May 1040 (great-seljuk-empire dossier).
wars.note: Not a Wikipedia title; the Seljuk dynasty page gives only 'the Seljuks defeated the Ghaznavids at the Battle of Nasa in 1035' and the Seljuk Empire page the 1037-1038 captures.

certainty.note: A tribal range on the Syr Darya and then a few Khorasan cities held by a nomadic army: no frontier is fixed on any page.

notes: Pages: Seljuk dynasty and Seljuk Empire (the budget of 1-2), plus Battle of Dandanaqan and Tughril, which were opened for the great-seljuk-empire dossier and are cited here only for the 1034 verdict. One state or two: Cliopatria's 'Seljuk Dynasty' (990-1039, Wikidata Q3708255) and 'Great Seljuk Empire' (1040-1201, Q3708094) are the same Seljuk state; the Seljuk Empire page dates its formation to 1037 under Tughril. The two dossiers hand over to each other at 1039|1040 and share the steppe family; a reviewer may merge them (a rename event). Cliopatria rows: the 990 start is five years after the page's 985; the 1034 shape (823,000 km2) is too large (Khwarezm, Golestan, the Turkmen plains) for what the pages attest; the 1037 keyframe replaces it from 1037. Page disagreements: the Seljuk dynasty page has Tughril abandon Cend in 1016 and also keeps Cend as the seat to 1037, and says the Great Seljuk Empire was 'established' after the 1050/51 siege of Isfahan while the Seljuk Empire page gives 1037/1040. The ledger year 1034 for the three ceded cities is from the Cliopatria shape (the Dandanaqan page says only 'after the battle'). Native names (Saljuqiyan, Selcuklular) are not on any page opened; they are given from general knowledge. The capital coordinates of Cend are approximate. Counterparts: the Oghuz Yabghu state is oghuz-turks (ia-01, which ends in 1055 in Cliopatria).
